name: Stop-Motion FPS Lag Texture
use_when: A smooth infographic sequence should feel handmade, editorial, or stop-motion-like.
A paper/chart/map sequence needs a unifying motion texture after timing is locked.
The project wants a subtle choppy cadence without rebuilding every keyframe.
A CapCut documentary collage needs a small amount of texture after the main scale, blur, and parallax motion are already readable.
avoid_when: The low-FPS effect makes text, map routes, chart bars, or small labels hard to read.
The style should feel premium-smooth, cinematic, or technically precise.
The sequence still needs timing changes, because global FPS texture can hide sync problems.

timeline_pattern.late_stage_rule: Apply the effect near the end of the graphic pass after internal animation timing is stable.
timeline_pattern.bypass_rule: Disable or reduce the effect on dense text/data moments if readability suffers.
timeline_pattern.style_rule: The effect should feel like editorial texture, not playback lag.

motion.rule: Use low-FPS texture to stylize motion cadence while preserving clear animation direction.

keyframe_values.capcut_fps_lag_speed: A speed value around 40 can create a strong choppy effect; tune down or bypass if text judders.
keyframe_values.capcut_subtle_fps_lag: A lower CapCut FPS Lag value around 14 can work as subtle documentary texture on a cutout collage after readability passes.
keyframe_values.posterize_range: For Remotion/AE equivalents, test 8-15 fps posterize-style cadence depending on readability.
keyframe_values.review_points: Check route reveals, chart labels, small text, and final title at normal speed after applying.

sound.rule: SFX should stay synced to visible motion after FPS texture is applied; recheck cue frames if the effect changes perceived timing.

captions.rule: Avoid applying heavy FPS texture to captions unless the caption style intentionally shares the choppy cadence and remains readable.

color.rule: No direct color rule; texture should not amplify compression artifacts in paper backgrounds or gradients.

implementation.ffmpeg: Approximate with fps or tblend/minterpolate choices on pre-rendered graphics; review for judder and text readability.
implementation.remotion: Use a posterizeTime-like frame sampling helper or render selected graphic components at lower update cadence while captions remain stable if needed.
implementation.blender: Render stepped keyframes or lower effective frame cadence for graphic elements, then inspect text readability.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Apply FPS Lag over the finished graphic timeline, start around speed 40, extend to the intended range, and bypass sections that become unreadable.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Posterize Time or frame-sampling effects on nested graphic sequences, not raw talking-head/caption sections unless intentionally stylized.

common_mistakes: Applying low-FPS texture before animation timing is finished.
Letting map or chart labels judder until they cannot be read.
Applying the effect to captions that should stay clean.
Using choppy motion to hide weak easing or bad keyframes.
Forgetting to recheck SFX sync after the cadence changes.
qc: Does the effect feel stylistic rather than like playback lag?
Are all maps, charts, documents, and labels still readable?
Are captions stable or intentionally stylized and readable?
Do SFX cues still feel synced to visible motion?
Are dense sections bypassed or reduced when the effect hurts comprehension?
